headline: Kordofan Giraffes Rebound in Congo Park After Poaching Crisis
meta_description: Garamba National Park's Kordofan giraffe population has surged from 22 to 105 since 2012, with zero poaching incidents since 2017.
summary_short: A Central African conservation success: endangered Kordofan giraffes in Garamba National Park have quintupled in 14 years, marking a major wildlife comeback.
body:
Garamba National Park in the Democratic Republic of Congo has achieved a remarkable conservation milestone: its Kordofan giraffe population has grown from just 22 animals in 2012 to 105 in 2026.

The recovery reflects years of dedicated protection work. The park has recorded no poaching incidents since 2017, a turning point that allowed the vulnerable population to rebuild. This progress stands out as one of Central Africa's most hopeful wildlife stories, offering evidence that endangered species can recover when given proper safeguards and sustained commitment.

The climb from fewer than two dozen giraffes to over one hundred represents not just a numerical gain, but a testament to the possibility of reversing species decline in regions where poaching and habitat loss have posed severe threats.
quick_facts: Kordofan giraffes in Garamba grew from 22 to 105 between 2012 and 2026
No recorded poaching since 2017 in Garamba National Park
Located in Democratic Republic of Congo, Central Africa
